h1: The 6 Best Google TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six Google TV sets from TCL and Hisense, from 55 to 85 inches, with refresh rates, panel types and who each one suits.
summary: The TCL 65-inch QM8K is the balanced choice for most living rooms. The TCL 75-inch QM8L adds a faster 144Hz panel at a bigger size, and the Hisense 55-inch U7 is the gaming pick for smaller rooms. The Hisense 85-inch U7 suits large spaces, and the CanvasTV S7 doubles as wall art.
intro: Picking a Google TV is mostly about matching screen size and refresh rate to the room, not about the operating system, which is the same across brands. The common mistake is buying a set that is too big for the viewing distance or paying for a refresh rate you will never use.

We reviewed six models from TCL and Hisense and ranked them on paper using size, refresh rate and panel type. Listings in this group give limited detail, so we kept claims to what the titles state. All sit in the $500+ bucket.

products.name: TCL 65 Inch Class QM8K Series
products.verdict: The most balanced size and spec mix in this group.
products.description:
The QM8K is a 65-inch QLED TV with a 120Hz panel, sold in the $500+ bucket.

The QM8K leads the list as 65 inches suits most living rooms and 120Hz covers sports and console play. The bigger QM8L adds a faster panel but also takes more wall.

A good default for a typical couch distance. The caveat is that the listing gives few other specs, so check the product page for HDMI details.
products.skipIf: You want a very large screen.

products.name: TCL 75 Inch Class QM8L Series
products.verdict: A bigger screen with a 144Hz panel.
products.description:
The QM8L is a 75-inch QLED set with a 144Hz panel, in the $500+ bucket.

The QM8L follows closely as it steps up both size and refresh rate over the QM8K. The trade is room: 75 inches wants a longer sofa distance.

Pick it for a big room and a gaming PC or console that can use 144Hz. Otherwise 120Hz is plenty.

products.name: Hisense 55" U7 Mini-LED ULED 4K UHD Best Premium Gaming Google Smart
products.verdict: A high-refresh set sized for smaller rooms.
products.description:
The 55-inch U7 is a Mini-LED ULED 4K set with a 165Hz panel, in the $500+ bucket.

The small U7 earns third place as 165Hz is the fastest here, but 55 inches is smaller than the TCL options. It is the right trade for a bedroom or small den.

Best for console and PC gamers. The caveat is that few video sources benefit from 165Hz.

products.name: Hisense 85" U7 Mini-LED ULED 4K UHD Best Premium Gaming Smart Google
products.verdict: The biggest screen here, with the same 165Hz panel.
products.description:
The 85-inch U7 pairs Mini-LED ULED 4K with a 165Hz panel, in the $500+ bucket.

The 85-inch U7 lands fourth as it is the largest screen but needs the most room, and the price rises accordingly compared with the 55-inch U7.

It suits a dedicated home theater. Measure the wall and doorways first.

products.name: Hisense 65“ Hi-QLED S7 CanvasTV Series 4K UHD Google Smart Art TV
products.verdict: A TV that is meant to look like wall art when off.
products.description:
The CanvasTV S7 is a 65-inch Hi-QLED 4K set with a 144Hz panel, positioned as an art TV, in the $500+ bucket.

The CanvasTV sits fifth as its art focus is a style choice rather than a picture-quality upgrade, so it sits below the performance-focused sets above.

Choose it if looks matter as much as specs. The listing gives few details about the art mode, so read the product page.
products.skipIf: You want the best picture per dollar.

products.name: TCL 75 Inch Class QM6K Series
products.verdict: A large 75-inch 120Hz set in a lower series.
products.description:
The QM6K is a 75-inch TCL with a 120Hz panel, in the $500+ bucket.

The QM6K ends the list as it sits below the QM8 series in TCL's lineup and the listing gives the least detail on its panel. It does offer a large size at 120Hz.

Best for buyers who want 75 inches without the QM8L's 144Hz. Verify the panel type on the product page before buying.
products.idealFor: Large-room buyers on a tighter budget.

whatMatters.detail: A common rule is to sit roughly one and a half times the screen diagonal away for 4K. A 65-inch set suits about eight feet, an 85-inch about ten. Measure your couch distance before choosing.
120Hz and above only help with sources that output that rate, such as consoles and PCs. Movies run at 24 frames. Check your consoles' output before paying for 144Hz or 165Hz.
QLED uses a quantum dot layer for color, while Mini-LED adds many small backlight zones for contrast. Look for the panel name in the listing title.
Google TV gives built-in streaming and voice search across brands. Confirm the title says Google, not an alternative platform.
Large sets need space for the wall and the doorway. Check the product page for stand width and weight.

cards.label: 120Hz
cards.text: Plenty for sports and most consoles. Picks: TCL QM8K and TCL QM6K.

cards.label: 144Hz to 165Hz
cards.text: Matters for PC and high-refresh console play. Picks: TCL QM8L, Hisense CanvasTV S7 and both Hisense U7 sets.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 120Hz or higher panel and a size that fits your seating distance.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Hisense 55" U7 offers 165Hz in a small body, and the TCL QM8K is the balanced 120Hz choice.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You game on PC or want a theater screen. The Hisense 85" U7 or TCL QM8L fit.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly stream. The TCL 75 Inch QM6K gives size without the top refresh rate.

faq.a: It is the smart TV platform built into these sets, offering streaming apps and voice search.

faq.q: What is a common buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing the biggest screen without measuring the room. Check viewing distance first.
Only for gaming sources that output high refresh. For streaming, 120Hz is enough.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Plug in, connect to WiFi and sign in with a Google account to download apps.

faq.q: How do I care for the screen?
faq.a: Wipe with a dry microfiber cloth and avoid spraying liquid on it.

faq.q: Is the Google TV Streamer a TV?
faq.a: No, it is a streaming box. We kept this ranking to TV sets.

finalTake: The TCL 65 Inch QM8K is the safest all-round buy. Gamers in small rooms should look at the Hisense 55" U7, and home theater buyers at the Hisense 85" U7. Decide on size and refresh rate first, then compare listings.
